clue.text: Trade embargo involving European broadcaster (6)

indicators.note: the embargo takes the broadcaster inside it

blocks.note: a bar = a ban, an embargo
RTE, Ireland's national broadcaster, goes between BA and R

explanation.surface: A news item about a ban that ropes in a TV station.
explanation.walkthrough: RTE (Raidió Teilifís Éireann) is Ireland's state broadcaster, so 'European' here means Irish.
explanation.definitionFit: To barter is to trade goods without money.

clue.text: A criminal ranger I'd put before a court (9)

indicators.note: the letters are behaving badly, out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A park ranger turned crook confesses he would be taken to court.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder sits either side of 'criminal', which works as the indicator while pretending to describe the ranger.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to bring someone before a court to answer a charge.

clue.text: Thanks number bringing in jelly (fruit) (7)

indicators.note: the number brings the jelly inside itself

blocks.note: gel = a jelly; it goes inside NO

explanation.surface: A thank-you for a jelly dish, with the fruit flavour noted in brackets.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta is everyday British for thanks. The bracketed '(fruit)' looks like a menu note but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus fruit, a cross between a tangerine and a pomelo.

clue.text: Broadcast TV series, missing last part, leaving you unsettled (7)

indicators.note: series drops its final letter
scattered, as seed is broadcast

explanation.surface: A TV series cut short before its finale leaves the audience restless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the TV surface perfectly but is the anagram indicator, in its sense of scattered widely.
explanation.definitionFit: Restive means restless, unable to keep still or settled.

clue.text: Battery supply getting energy for some computer storage (8)

indicators.note: read as supple-ly: the letters bend into a new shape
the battery letters take on the E

explanation.surface: A battery supply powering some computer data storage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is not the noun but an adverb: supply, in a supple way. That pliant sense is what makes it an anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A terabyte is a unit of computer storage, about a trillion bytes.

clue.text: Nerdy letterhead redesigned in compassionate style (6-9)

indicators.note: the letters are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A geeky letterhead gets a makeover in a kindly style.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about stationery design, so 'redesigned' reads as literal while also telling you to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting tender-heartedly is acting with compassion.

clue.text: Lay claim to additional military support (7)

blocks.note: a verb: to book or stake a claim to something in advance, as with a seat
a noun: troops held back behind the front line, ready to be sent in

explanation.surface: An army staking a claim to extra backup forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses meet at 'to': one a verb, one a noun, and the surface runs them into a single military sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve something is to claim it in advance; a reserve is extra military force held back.

clue.text: Too demeaning for queen, say, to receive knight at home initially (7)

indicators.note: the queen takes the knight inside
only the first letter of home

blocks.note: a queen is one example of a bee
N = knight in chess notation; it goes inside BEE

explanation.surface: A royal refusing to host a knight at her home as beneath her dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' wants to be a monarch, and the royal surface backs that up; the 'say' shows it is an example, here a queen bee.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the idiom 'beneath one's dignity': a chore too lowly for someone to stoop to.

clue.text: Earldom? Earl supports it amidst foremost in the Lords (5)

indicators.note: IT goes in the middle of the two letters
take the first letter of each word
in a down answer, the earl sits underneath, holding up the rest

blocks.note: as printed; it goes inside TL
E = earl, as in peerage abbreviations

explanation.surface: A question about a peerage, answered with an earl's standing in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks earldom as just one example of the answer. 'Supports' places E at the bottom of a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by the question mark: an earldom is one kind of hereditary rank a peer holds.

clue.text: Ex-students working to welcome new member of later generation (8)

indicators.note: the ex-students take the new letter in

blocks.note: N = new; it goes inside GRADS

explanation.surface: Alumni at work greeting a younger recruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New member' reads as one phrase in the surface, but 'new' is N for the wordplay and 'member of later generation' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandson belongs to the generation two down from his grandparents.

clue.text: Contribution to concerts on at Aldeburgh? (6)

definitions.text: Contribution to concerts on at Aldeburgh?

indicators.note: the answer is a part given by the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of concerts, the words on and at, and the start of Aldeburgh

explanation.surface: A programme item at the Aldeburgh music festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldeburgh is a Suffolk seaside town with a famous classical music festival founded by Benjamin Britten, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a piece that might well feature in a classical concert.

clue.text: It really shouldn't be found amongst capitals of nations in Central Europe! (4)

definitions.text: It really shouldn't be found amongst capitals of nations in Central Europe!

indicators.note: capital letters: the first letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of nations, in, Central, Europe

explanation.surface: A geography teacher's warning about a city that is out of place on a list of Central European capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is a city on the French Riviera, neither a capital nor in Central Europe, yet it is spelt out by the 'capitals' of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice is a French city that is not a capital and lies nowhere near Central Europe.

clue.text: Ship prompting discussion? (10)

definitions.note: 'prompting discussion' describes what an icebreaker does; the answer is the noun

blocks.note: a ship built to cut through sea ice
an opening remark or game that gets people talking

explanation.surface: A vessel that gets everyone talking.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that the second half is a loose description of a conversational icebreaker rather than a strict synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebreaker is both a ship that clears ice and something that starts people talking.

clue.text: Chief not mistaken - it's crucial for many jobs these days (8)

definitions.text: it's crucial for many jobs these days

indicators.note: the letters are in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A boss insisting he is right about what modern jobs need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not mistaken' reads as one phrase meaning correct, but the break falls after 'not': that word is fodder and 'mistaken' the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Infotech, information technology, underpins a great many modern jobs.

clue.text: What helps to coat a road? (3)

definitions.text: What helps to coat a road?

indicators.note: the answer is part of the words that follow

blocks.note: the last letter of coat, the word a, and the first letter of road

explanation.surface: A question about road-surfacing materials.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: tar really does help coat a road, and it sits inside those words.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar is used, with stone chips, to surface roads.

clue.text: Reflects European votes, one with second Conservative ousted (6)

indicators.note: one and the second C are thrown out

blocks.clueFragment: votes, one with second Conservative ousted
blocks.note: CHOICES loses I (one) and its second C (Conservative)

explanation.surface: An election result mirroring European voting after a Tory is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' tells you which C goes: CHOICES has two, and only the later one is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo is to reflect sound, or to repeat an idea.

clue.text: What suggests you perform treatment doctor ultimately dismissed? (3)

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so it points to the doctor's final letter
something dismissed is sent away, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: last letter of doctor, removed from CURE

explanation.surface: A patient asking what prompts a treatment once the doctor has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical surface pulls 'treatment' and 'doctor' together, but the definition is the theatrical sense at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is the signal telling an actor or musician to perform.

clue.text: A spirit otherwise not special and wild (9)

indicators.note: 'not special' means lacking special, so the S that stands for it is taken away

explanation.surface: A ghost described as unusual and untamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' and 'special' look like descriptions of the spirit, but both are wordplay, and 'A spirit' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An elemental is a spirit of one of the four elements, such as a sylph or salamander.

clue.text: One of several kings in conflict, surrounded by endless revolution (6)

indicators.note: a thing surrounded by another is enclosed within it, so the conflict sits inside
without an end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: EDDY = a whirl, a revolution, without its last letter
war = conflict; it goes inside EDD

explanation.surface: A king caught up in war and ceaseless rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests uprising in the royal surface, but here it is a swirling motion, an eddy.
explanation.definitionFit: England has had eight kings called Edward.

clue.text: Referred everyone to unreliable dude (7)

indicators.note: the letters cannot be trusted to stay in order

explanation.surface: Someone passed everybody on to a flaky guy.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'referred' and 'to' look like the phrase 'referred to', but 'Referred' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude to something is to refer to it indirectly.

clue.text: Severe pressure sees loss of University Hospital department worker in theatre (7)

indicators.note: to see the loss of something is to go without it, so the U is taken out

blocks.clueFragment: Severe pressure sees loss of University

explanation.surface: A university hospital under strain losing a member of the operating theatre staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The hospital surface makes 'theatre' an operating theatre; the answer is a backstage worker who helps actors into costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser helps performers with their costumes in the theatre.

clue.text: English composer's securing hideaway in French department (8)

indicators.note: the composer holds the hideaway inside

blocks.note: Thomas Arne, composer of 'Rule, Britannia!', plus 's
a den = a hideaway; it goes inside ARNES

explanation.surface: An English composer bags a secret retreat in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Arne is the crossword's favourite English composer. The Ardennes is a French département on the Belgian border.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardennes is one of France's numbered administrative departments.

clue.text: US author reinterpreted desire, right? (7)

indicators.note: the letters are read in a new way

explanation.surface: A critic's new reading of desire in an American writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Theodore Dreiser wrote 'Sister Carrie' and 'An American Tragedy', novels much concerned with desire, which is what makes the surface ring true.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore Dreiser was an American novelist.

clue.text: Significantly, no boat's prow getting left in river (7)

indicators.note: a ship's prow is its front: the first letter
B and L go inside the river

blocks.note: L = left; B and L go inside TAY

explanation.surface: A boat without a bow ends up abandoned in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Significantly, no' reads as a phrase, but the comma is the break: the definition is the adverb alone. The Tay is Scotland's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: Notably means significantly, in a way worth noting.

clue.text: Place with lots of phones but only one line, it seems (4,6)

definitions.text: Place with lots of phones but only one line, it seems

blocks.note: the straight reading: an office packed with telephones and staff

blocks.clueFragment: but only one line, it seems
blocks.note: the paradox: many phones yet one line, which is the script every operator repeats

explanation.surface: An office stuffed with telephones that nonetheless answers with the same patter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' plays on phone line and on a line of patter: every operator seems to repeat the same scripted line.
explanation.definitionFit: A call centre is an office where many staff handle phone calls.

clue.text: Do I seem to be ready, friend? (5)

blocks.note: go = ready, as in 'all systems go'

explanation.surface: Someone checking with a pal that they look ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do I seem to be ready?' becomes 'Am I go?', with 'go' in its sense of ready and working.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, used informally in English.

clue.text: Limits to timber expanse? Here's one of them (4)

definitions.text: Limits to timber expanse? Here's one of them

indicators.note: the outside letters of each word

blocks.note: first and last letters of timber
first and last letters of expanse

explanation.surface: A question about where a forest stops, answered by one of its trees.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'timber expanse' is a forest, so 'one of them' makes the whole clue the definition as well as the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest is made up of trees, so a tree is one of its parts.

clue.text: Members of religious group back America (6)

blocks.note: hind = back, as in hind legs

explanation.surface: Worshippers who back America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a verb or a reversal instruction, but it is the adjective hind.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain description: the religious group is Hinduism, and its adherents are its members.

clue.text: Dry cleaning? It's for the birds! (4-4)

definitions.text: Dry cleaning? It's for the birds!

blocks.note: the surface pushes the laundry service; the setter means a wash done without water
an idiom for worthless, but read literally: sparrows and hens roll in dry earth to clean their feathers

explanation.surface: A put-down of the laundry service: dry cleaning is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's for the birds' is an idiom for worthless, which is why the dry-cleaning surface sounds like a complaint; read literally, it is about birds bathing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust bath is a bird's roll in dry dust to clean its feathers.

clue.text: Firm way with your tatty fabric (8)

indicators.note: ragged, the letters in disarray

explanation.surface: A firm, blunt remark about someone's scruffy clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' passes for an adjective of manner in the surface; in the wordplay it is a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the ribbed cotton cloth is one kind of fabric, and tatty old cords fit the surface.

clue.text: Ruling group: type mostly holding place back (6)

indicators.note: most but not all of the word, so the last letter is dropped
to hold something is to keep it within your grasp, so SOR takes LAY inside
going back means going backwards, so the whole is then read in reverse

blocks.note: SORT = type, without its last letter
to lay = to place; it goes inside SOR after the S

explanation.surface: A political faction holding its ground while being pushed back.
explanation.walkthrough: SOR holding LAY makes SLAYOR, which read backwards is ROYALS.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose description: the royal family is the group that rules, at least nominally, in a monarchy.
